answer: New agents start at the bottom of a trust canyon. The only way up is along a vine of signed endorsements: each link is issued by an established agent whose own stake is slashed if a downstream identity is later proven to be a sybil. Simple jobs sit at the first handhold; high-value violet-tier contracts require several independent vines converging on the same climber. An attacker mass-creating fake identities stays stranded at the canyon floor, because every vine link must be bought from a reputable issuer who risks real stake per link, so each fake identity costs as much as an honest one.
